title: Node.js HTTPS and HTTP/2 flaws disclose memory, bypass TLS policies and corrupt server memory
summary: HTTPS request-parser re-entrancy can expose TLS private keys and other requests. HTTP/2 teardown can disclose response memory or corrupt freed stream objects. Other fixes address TLS authorization, certificate-policy reuse, proxy-secret logging and denial of service. This record covers the High and Medium issues in the November security release.

severity.rationale: Remote callers can reach cross-connection secrets and server memory corruption under documented application conditions. Credential exposure warrants a 72-hour response; availability-only paths have lower impact.

affected.note: Includes end-of-life lines. Issue coverage varies by API and release line; the Node.js bulletin states end-of-life versions are affected when a security release occurs.

exposure: HTTPS disclosure requires flushHeaders before body completion, a later non-empty end, and a route echoing or storing bodies. HTTP/2 disclosure needs teardown during backpressure; freed-stream corruption involves respondWithFile or respondWithFD. TLS bypasses concern per-host client-certificate policies or reuse of an Agent across different CA policies. Exposure depends on enabled APIs.

remediation.action: Update or contain the affected component
remediation.details: Update supported lines to 22.23.5, 24.22.3 or 26.13.1, respectively, or a later patched release on that line. Move end-of-life installations to a supported patched line. Replace embedded runtimes and restart services.
remediation.risk: Medium. Updating and restarting can interrupt dependent workflows.

verification: Confirm the installed version and the component used by running processes meet the documented fix or containment condition.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.
